text:
sam_k: hey! new hire question. running `docker compose up -d` then `docker compose run --rm web rails db:create` but the `web` run fails to connect to postgres: `PG::ConnectionBad: could not connect to server: Connection refused` — db service is up and `docker compose ps` shows db healthy. why does run not see the db?

olga: welcome! common trap: `docker compose run` creates a new container that by default does not use the same network as `up` services unless you target the compose project network. Also `run` doesn't start linked depends unless `--service-ports`/`--use-aliases` used.

sam_k: ah interesting. I thought `run` would join the compose network. What should I do instead?

olga: easiest: use `docker compose exec web rails db:create` if the `web` service is already running. If you need a one-off container, do `docker compose run --service-ports --entrypoint "sh" web` then run rake inside that shell — or explicitly join the network: `docker compose run --rm --network $(docker compose ps -q db | xargs docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.NetworkID}}{{end}}') web` (a bit ugly).

dev-tools-bot: dev-tools-bot posted: "Tip: prefer `exec` for running commands in an existing service container; `run` is for ephemeral containers and may not share volumes/networks by default."

peter: also check your DATABASE_URL in .env. If it's set to host.docker.internal it won't resolve inside containers to the db service. For in-compose calls use `postgres://postgres:password@db:5432/app_development`. Host mappings (localhost/host.docker.internal) are only for host -> container connections.

sam_k: switched to `docker compose exec web rails db:create` and it worked. thanks both — will update my notes. Two quick follow-ups: 1) should onboarding doc mention `exec` vs `run`? 2) any recommended pattern for one-off jobs?

olga: yes add a short note. For one-offs we usually add a `Makefile` target: `make run-console` which uses `docker compose run --rm --service-ports web` so it inherits the compose network and ports. Keeps things consistent for new hires.

sam_k: perfect, will open a tiny PR. thanks for the quick help! :tada:
